newsitem.title: USA: USWC light crudes continue down, buyers watch Oct.
newsitem.headline: USWC light crudes continue down, buyers watch Oct.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes continued lower late on Friday, with September business finished and refiners deferring deals until they decide how much crude they need in October.
October West Texas Intermediate fell on a bearish combination of renewed imports from the North Sea and Mexico and lightened demand after shippers reserved pipeline space.
That left October WTI 30 cents below Thursday at $21.90/22.00 a barrel.
Refiners reported adequate inventories for September Alaskan crude and began to focus on October shipments.
Early on Thursday, the dominant ANS producer sold to a Hawaiian refiner at $2.05 a barrel under October WTI, 10 cents lower than the previous sale.
Atlantic Richfield Co denied market rumours from late Thursday and early today that its Ferndale, Washington refinery suffered an outage.
Prices for Line 63 slipped with WTI, and spot deals off WTI remained dormant.
Kern River and Wilmington grades were unchanged late.
